subject: Order form — commercial carve-up, invoicing route & tax evidence
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>
To: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwoodinference.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Sarah Jenkins <sarah.jenkins@pulsehealth.com>, Procurement PulseHealth <procurement@pulsehealth.com>
Date: 2028-04-02T08:12:00-07:00
Subject: Order form — commercial carve-up, invoicing route & tax evidence

Team / Pulse procurement,

Attaching the latest order form (Pulse_OrderForm_v3.pdf). Pulse is asking us to: 1) confirm which Redwood entity will receive payments for EU invoices, 2) accept net45 as requested by their AP team, and 3) confirm VAT handling (they asked about reverse-charge).

Key commercial points in the doc: pricing schedule with phased minimum commit (Q1: 40%, Q2: 30%, Q3–4: 30%), currency in EUR for EU invoices, and an optional advance invoice for the first tranche.

Can finance confirm whether we can invoice Redwood EU (our EMEA entity) and take reverse-charge with their VAT ID? Also legal: any concerns with the net45 ask or the suggested invoice split across entities?

Requested next steps:
- Kimberly: confirm invoicing entity and whether we can grant net45 (or require net30 with escalation).
- Grace / Legal: quick check on MSA cross-entity language for tax/residency.
- Karthik: ping procurement to get PO number and VAT ID if available.

Thanks — Ben

Attachments:
- Pulse_OrderForm_v3.pdf (Order form draft)

From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwoodinference.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Sarah Jenkins <sarah.jenkins@pulsehealth.com>, Procurement PulseHealth <procurement@pulsehealth.com>
Date: 2028-04-02T10:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Order form — commercial carve-up, invoicing route & tax evidence

Thanks Ben — looping in finance + legal. A few clarifying points before we redline: 

1) Minimum commit phasing: the order form currently allocates the 12-month commitment across one commercial bucket. We should call out the tranche amounts and whether missed tranches roll forward or credit. Finance: please advise language we should require for proration / carry-forward.

2) Invoicing entity fallback: ideal is to invoice PulseHealth EU (so invoices are in EUR and subject to reverse-charge), but we need to confirm the VAT ID and an AP mailbox. If they cannot provide an EU VAT ID in time, proposed fallback is: invoice Redwood US for the first tranche (advance invoice) and then re-invoice to EU once VAT evidence arrives. Is that operationally acceptable? 

3) Net terms: Procurement asked for net45. Our standard is net30; we can consider net45 for enterprise if we add an SLA/credit clause to protect cash. Kimberly — can you run scenario on cash impact for net45 vs net30 for the first two tranches? Also, if we accept net45, we should require PO number on the invoice and attach a short payment schedule to the order form.

4) Tax evidence: please use the attached VAT evidence template (I will send it) — ask Pulse to populate and return. If they indicate reverse-charge, ask for both VAT ID and company registration country.

I'll prepare a light redline of the order form focusing on the invoice recipient, PO requirement, and a fallback invoicing path. Karthik — please push procurement for VAT ID and the AP mailbox.

Best,
Grace

Date: 2028-04-02T14:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Order form — commercial carve-up, invoicing route & tax evidence

Grace / team,

Quick finance view: we can invoice from Redwood EMEA (our UK entity) and accept reverse-charge, provided Pulse returns a valid EU VAT registration number and confirms the legal entity name matches. Operational asks: we need the VAT ID, a signed PO number on the first invoice, and the AP mailbox to send PDF invoices.

Notes / proposals:
- Net terms: we typically do net30. Net45 is acceptable for strategic accounts but requires an approval from Finance (I can approve for up to €250k exposure). For larger exposure we should escalate to FP&A.
- Advance invoice: recommend we issue an advance invoice for the first tranche equal to the Q1 minimum (40%), payable on receipt. If Pulse needs net45 on that advance invoice, we should add an interest clause (1.5% monthly after 60 days) or require a short-term credit hold.
- Currency / FX: if they pay in EUR but our ledger is USD, include a simple clause that invoices show both EUR amount and an indicative USD conversion rate (we don't accept FX risk beyond a 2% variance without explicit agreement).

I'm attaching a VAT evidence template that we can send to Pulse to collect: vat_evidence_template.xlsx

If Pulse can provide VAT ID by end of week, we can keep invoicing to the EU entity. Otherwise, fallback to Redwood US for the first invoice as Grace suggested (we will then issue credit/adjustment once evidence arrives).

Kimberly
Finance, Redwood Inference

Hi Grace / Ben / Kim,

Thanks for the quick turnaround. Procurement confirms: we can provide the EU VAT ID and the AP mailbox, and procurement has issued PO_4521_PulseHealth.pdf (attached). Our AP team prefers net45 for payment terms. 

A couple of asks from our side: 
- Can Redwood accept the EU VAT ID under the reverse-charge mechanism and include the VAT ID on the invoice?
- For the first tranche, we would like the invoice to reference PO_4521 and be sent to pulse-ap@pulsehealth.com.
- On credits / FX: procurement would like a clause for currency fluctuation protection (example: +/-3% band), otherwise they prefer invoices in EUR only.

Attached: PO_4521_PulseHealth.pdf

We will push legal to be light on MSA redlines; procurement prefers quick execution. Happy to supply VAT docs by EOD.

Best,
Sarah

Thanks all — summary and next steps below. I uploaded a light redline of the order form (Pulse_OrderForm_v3_redlined.pdf) to the Drive and attached here.

Summary of agreements / open items:
- Pulse will provide EU VAT ID and AP mailbox (Sarah to send VAT docs EOD).
- Finance can invoice from Redwood EMEA and accept reverse-charge on receipt of valid VAT ID. Kimberly approved net45 for this deal up to €250k exposure; we will escalate if exposure exceeds that.
- We will issue an advance invoice for the Q1 tranche (40%) to Pulse AP referencing PO_4521. If payment terms are net45 on advance, Finance has flagged a 1.5% monthly interest after 60 days; we will keep that as an escalation-only clause and prefer not to apply by default.
- FX / currency: invoices will be issued in EUR. We will include an indicative USD conversion but will not assume FX above a 2% variance; procurement may propose +/-3% — note for legal.

Action items (owner / ETA):
- Sarah / Pulse: send VAT ID + VAT evidence by EOD (owner: Pulse)
- Karthik: confirm receipt of PO_4521 and forward PDF to billing@redwoodinference.com (ETA: today)
- Kimberly: finalize payment exposure approval and confirm whether interest clause language is acceptable (ETA: COB tomorrow)
- Ben / Legal: review redlined order form for MSA cross-entity language and confirm no new commercial risk (ETA: 48 hours)
- Grace: prepare DocuSign package once redline accepted (DocuSign link: https://app.docusign.com/recipient/12345-OrderForm-Pulse)

If everyone is aligned, I'll move the redline into DocuSign and ask Pulse to sign. Thanks for the fast responses.

Regards,
Grace O'Connor
Head of Commercial Ops
Redwood Inference

Attachments:
- Pulse_OrderForm_v3_redlined.pdf
- vat_evidence_template.xlsx (referenced)
